observations.body: James names royal neighbor-love, partiality, the unity of law, adultery and murder, judgment by a law of liberty, and mercy over judgment.
observations.label: Neighbor-love, partiality, and commands form a law of liberty argument

observations.body: Neighbor-love, partiality, and commands form a law of liberty argument belongs to sinai remembered in the Sinai trail.
observations.label: Where this sits

observations.body: James 2:8–13 supplies later-memory evidence for the event’s developing sequence.
observations.label: Within the Sinai event

observations.body: Later witnesses select and reuse Sinai in their own settings; they remain later readings rather than replacements for the Exodus event.
observations.label: Reading boundary

payload.posture: Read James 2:8–13 as its own source before carrying it into the wider Sinai trail.
payload.tension: Neighbor-love, partiality, and commands form a law of liberty argument belongs to the sinai remembered movement, but its part in the event must remain distinct from the surrounding speech, response, breach, and renewal.
payload.title: Neighbor-love, partiality, and commands form a law of liberty argument
